pages.text: The flagpole on Dad's boat was empty. Mom gave them a piece of white cloth.
They wanted to make a flag for Dad's boat. "It is our boat's flag, so let us paint a fish!"
They held opposite sides of the cloth. Riri held her brush delicately upright; Lolo soaked a brush in paint. "We should paint all the scales." "We should paint the sea first."
Riri painted scales one by one. Tiny scales appeared in rows.
The sun was overhead, but only half a fish was done. She had not even started the tail.
Lolo poured blue paint across the cloth. It turned entirely blue.
Paint dripped, leaving blotches. "My fish!" "My sea!" They pulled at the cloth.
It slipped out of their hands and caught on the clothesline. They looked up from underneath.
The blue blotches looked like rolling waves. Half a fish swam over them.
The flag rose on Dad's flagpole. In the wind, the fish seemed really to swim—even without a tail.
